menu.cover: Opening slide of a deck: title and one-sentence subtitle only.
menu.section: Divider that starts a new part of a long deck (8+ slides): part number and name.
menu.split/text+number: Short argument on the left, ONE big number on the right that proves it (a market size, a cost, a gap).
menu.split/chart+notes: Chart on the left two-thirds, 2-4 numbered observations on the right, each can pin a data point. For a chart that needs explaining.
menu.full/chart: One full-width chart. For a chart the title alone explains.
menu.split/table+notes: Table (up to 4 columns) on the left two-thirds, 2-4 observations on the right. For exact figures that need interpretation.
menu.full/table: One full-width table (up to 5 columns, up to 8 rows). For exact figures to compare across rows.
menu.full/steps: 2-5 steps in time: a plan, roadmap, process or history.
menu.row/cards: 2-4 parallel cards side by side, each led by an icon or a big value: options, pillars, features, several independent numbers, or a two-way contrast (them vs us, before vs after).

guide: Answer in order and stop at the first match:
1. The first slide of a deck -> cover.
2. The start of a new part in a deck of 8+ slides -> section.
3. ONE number that proves the argument -> split/text+number.
4. Data over categories or time (a series) that needs 2-4 observations or pinned points to be understood -> split/chart+notes.
5. Data over categories or time that the title alone explains -> full/chart.
6. Exact figures to compare, up to 4 columns, that need interpretation -> split/table+notes.
7. Exact figures to compare, or 5 columns, or more than 6 rows -> full/table.
8. A sequence in time: plan, roadmap, process, history (2-5 steps) -> full/steps.
9. 2-4 parallel things: options, pillars, features, several independent numbers, or a two-way contrast -> row/cards.

Tie-breakers: Chart when the point is a trend, a comparison of sizes or a crossover; table when the reader needs exact values. Add notes only if each note says something the chart or table does not show; in pitch prefer the variant without notes. Several independent numbers -> row/cards; one decisive number -> split/text+number. When in doubt, pick the entry with fewer words.
